title: Abhimanyu in the Chakravyuha
text:
On the thirteenth day of the great war at Kurukshetra, Drona, commanding the Kaurava army, arranged his troops in the chakravyuha, a formation of rings within rings that few warriors knew how to break. Arjuna, who did know, had been drawn away to fight elsewhere on the field.

Yudhishthira turned to Arjuna's young son Abhimanyu, a brilliant fighter, and asked him to break the formation. Abhimanyu answered that he knew how to force his way into it, but if trouble came, he did not know how to get out. Yudhishthira and Bhima promised to follow right behind him through the breach and protect him.

Abhimanyu charged, and he broke into the circle. But as the Pandava warriors rushed to follow, Jayadratha, king of the Sindhus, held the gap and drove them back. Abhimanyu was alone inside.

He fought with astonishing courage, killing many warriors. Finally several great fighters attacked him together. They broke his bow, killed his horses and his charioteer, and destroyed his chariot. He fought on with a sword and then with a chariot wheel. At last, exhausted and surrounded, he was struck down and killed.
lesson: Before you commit to a bold move, plan your way out as carefully as your way in, and do not rely on support that someone else must break through to deliver.
people: Abhimanyu, Yudhishthira, Drona, Jayadratha, the Kaurava warriors
